raw_response:
Well, I've been farming these 3 mu for forty years now, so I pretty much know what to do. It's just me and my wife at home — the kids are in the city working — so we manage everything ourselves. Three mu isn't much, but it feeds us and brings in a little cash.

For the wheat, I'll plant around the 10th of October like always, after I clear the maize stalks. I usually buy Jimai 22 seed from the agricultural supply shop — about 15 kg per mu sowing rate. Before planting I spread about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu (that's the 15-15-15 kind) as a base. Then come spring, when the wheat greens up and starts jointing around late March, I topdress urea — maybe 15 kg per mu. The extension fellow once told me 12 kg was enough but I've always done a bit more, and my wheat does fine at around 450 kg per mu most years.

Water — I irrigate from the tube well. Winter watering in late November if the soil is dry, then at jointing, then at heading. Three times usually, maybe four if it's a dry spring. Pumping costs money, so I don't water if it rained recently.

For maize, the turnaround is tight. The day after I harvest wheat in early June, I'm out there with no-till planting — I hire the neighbor who owns the planter, costs me maybe 30 yuan per mu. I plant Zhengdan 958, it's reliable. Base fertilizer goes in with the seed, then one topdress of urea at the big-trumpet stage, maybe 15 kg per mu. One irrigation usually, at tasseling if it's dry. Expect about 500 kg per mu.

Herbicide I use on both crops — one spray after planting. Don't bother with insecticide unless I actually see armyworms or something. At my age I can't be spraying without a reason.
